subtallies.name: May a product sit on a non-leaf node?
cells: Walmart (no tree — the feed takes exactly one product type)
Tokopedia Era A (leaf rule implied by a call-sequence label only)

framing: The shape of the split is the finding: every platform in the (b) column is a marketplace with a centrally-authored tree, and every platform in the (a) column either authors nothing (Google, Walmart) or hands the tree to the merchant — with Shopify and Amazon the two that author centrally AND still permit it. Card corrections: Walmart has no category tree to be leafy; Tokopedia's eras must be separated. The observed seller response to leaf-only is to reach for an “… > Other” leaf — exactly the structure our tree already has (44 used catch-all nodes, 3,591 products, 32 of them leaves).

rows.shape: “Yes — no leaf-only rule; ‘most specific’ is worded as a performance caution.” Placement is a BrowseNode id chosen from an enum inside the product type's schema.

rows.h: a live write, not a doc reading
rows.shape: “Yes — product created on aa-1-13, isLeaf:false, userErrors:[].” Inference: permitting it costs nothing because the per-node attribute list exists at every level — only 152 of 14,606 nodes have none.

“Yes — discouraged, never forbidden; of 20 ids Google names as submission targets, 14 are parents.” Stated: “All products are automatically assigned a product category from Google's continuously evolving product taxonomy… [google_product_category] can be used to override Google's automatic categorization in specific cases.” Inference: a leaf rule on a field the platform fills for you would be incoherent.

rows.h: stated on three surfaces, two collected live 2026-09-19
rows.shape: Error 62009, 400, API_TAXONOMY/REQUEST: “The specified category ID must be a leaf category.” EDP guide (P0, 200,027 B): “Every eBay listing must be listed in an eBay leaf category.” File Exchange error 87: “Invalid Category. The category selected is not a leaf category. | Listing will fail.” Inference, heavily evidenced: the leaf id is the key for every per-category policy lookup (item conditions, aspects, parts compatibility, Best-Offer eligibility, identifier policy); mitigation is getCategorySuggestions. What sellers do: reach for an “… > Other” leaf (community thread, 3Dsellers help page — S5 lead).

rows.h: the “no” is about a flat product-type field, not leafness
rows.shape: “No — the feed takes exactly one product type”; “no category field in the feed at all.” Not collected: why the feed carries no category field (route: the MP_ITEM spec's overview, in the 451 MB corpus not on this machine).
“Please note that only the category_id with has_children = false can be used to create or update products.”

rows.h: Era B stated; Era A ambiguous
rows.shape: Era B: “It must be a leaf category that corresponds to the category tree type specified in the category_version property.” Era A: the vendor's call sequence step 1 is GET …/product/category → leaf category id; no rule sentence retrieved.
“Yes — the vendor's own example categorises items as ‘Clothing’, the root.”
“No leaf rule in any artifact; a vendor fixture assigns a product to root, which has a child.”

“Category yes by default, with a per-tree only_leaves setting that makes it leaf-only.” Inference: leaf-only as a setting is what you ship when the tree is the merchant's — the vendor cannot know whether a customer's tree is a partition or a facet hierarchy.
“Yes — an ordinary wp_term_relationships row; nothing tests leafness.”
“Yes — leaf occurs 0 times in 5,366,096 B of spec.”
